solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Rarely has one topic that one can crack

indicators.note: rarely read as 'in a rare or unusual way', telling us to arrange these letters unusually

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A grumble that someone seldom gets a subject they can really get to grips with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rarely' looks like an adverb about how often, but it signals the anagram of HAS, I and TOPIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistachio is a nut, and nuts are what people crack open to eat.

clue.text: Academic briefly leading appeal to make money

indicators.note: leading says the first piece goes in front of the second
briefly says the word is cut short, keeping only its familiar opening

parts.note: an academic may be a professor
it is old slang for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A lecturer cuts short to make a fundraising pitch for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: To profit is to gain financially, to come out ahead in money.

clue.text: Editor and writer beginning to recognise their paying customer?

parts.note: a sub, short for sub-editor, edits copy on a newspaper
a scribe is a writer

indicators.note: beginning to picks the opening letter of the word recognise

explanation.surface: Newspaper staff learn to acknowledge the reader who pays for them.
explanation.definitionFit: A subscriber pays regularly for a magazine or service, a paying customer.

clue.text: Like ultra-spiritual type that offers response to disease?

definitions.text: Like ultra-spiritual type that offers response to disease?

parts.words: Like ultra-spiritual type that offers response to disease?
parts.note: an ultra-spiritual type might be said to be against the body; split the answer into two words to see it, then read it whole as the immune system's agent

explanation.surface: A mystic so spiritual they reject the flesh is offered as a remedy for illness.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as ANTI-BODY, the answer describes someone opposed to the physical body; whole, it is the protein the immune system makes against infection.
explanation.definitionFit: Antibodies are proteins produced by the immune system in response to infection.

clue.text: The fellow facing destiny as a lowly worker

indicators.note: facing puts the first piece in front of, looking at, the second

parts.note: the fellow is he
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A man confronts his fate of being a humble labourer.
explanation.definitionFit: A helot was a serf in ancient Sparta, hence any downtrodden labourer.

clue.text: Squander cash on account of what bookie offers? Then stop!

parts.note: over can mean because of, as in 'a row over money'
SP is the starting price, the odds a bookmaker offers at the start of a race
to end is to stop

explanation.surface: Advice to a gambler: waste your money on the odds, then quit.
explanation.walkthrough: A bookie is a bookmaker, who takes bets on horse races in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To overspend is to pay out more than one can afford, wasting money.

clue.text: Soft device for fixing shrub

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft
a rivet is a metal pin for fastening plates together

explanation.surface: A gentle tool for mending a bush.
explanation.definitionFit: Privet is an evergreen bush widely planted as garden hedging.

clue.text: Wild animal in European capital starts to scare Brits off

indicators.note: off says those letters are taken away from the capital

parts.note: Lisbon is the capital of Portugal

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letter of each of scare and Brits

explanation.surface: A beast loose in a European city frightens off British tourists.
explanation.definitionFit: The lion is a big cat of the African savannah, a wild beast.

clue.text: Most inadequate hotel and pub exposed in inspection

indicators.note: the hotel and pub are revealed sitting in the middle of the inspection word

parts.note: a test is an examination or inspection
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A hotel and its bar found badly wanting by the inspectors.
explanation.definitionFit: Thinnest means flimsiest, as an excuse or argument that is weakest.

clue.text: Disappear, having crossed river in Japan?

definitions.note: japan as a verb means to coat with hard glossy lacquer

indicators.note: the first word stretches across the river letter, holding it inside

parts.note: to vanish is to disappear

explanation.surface: Someone vanishes after crossing a river in Japan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japan' looks like a country, but lower-case japan is a black lacquer and the verb to coat with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To japan a surface is to lacquer it, which is to give it a glossy coat.

clue.text: Sort of road test after component has been installed

indicators.note: the component is fitted inside the test word

parts.note: an oral is a spoken examination
a bit is a part or component

explanation.surface: A road test carried out once a car part has been fitted.
explanation.walkthrough: An orbital is a British ring road circling a city, like London's M25.
explanation.definitionFit: An orbital road is a ring road going round a city.

clue.text: Poison in ancient city going round he got rid of

indicators.note: got rid of says the word he is removed
going round tells us to turn the city name back to front

parts.note: Nineveh was the capital of ancient Assyria
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man disposed of poison while touring an old city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going round' turns the city into HEVENIN; 'got rid of' then drops the HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Venin is a toxic substance found in snake venom.

clue.text: In island country group in retreat broods

parts.note: Cuba is a Caribbean island nation

indicators.note: in retreat says the group word is read backwards

parts.note: a set is a group

explanation.surface: A band falls back on a Caribbean island and sulks.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird incubates its eggs by sitting on them, which is to brood.

clue.text: Like a drink and place for serving food by river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
a table is where food is served

explanation.surface: A drink and a dining spot beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Potable water is safe to drink, so potable means drinkable.

clue.text: Command to invade indistinctive territory close to another country

indicators.note: the command enters the middle of the word for indistinctive

parts.note: bland means lacking distinctive character
an order is a command

explanation.surface: Orders to invade a dull stretch of land near a frontier.
explanation.definitionFit: A borderland is the district lying along a frontier.

clue.text: Reportedly, put out to search for water

indicators.note: reportedly says we hear the word rather than see it spelt

parts.note: to douse a fire is to put it out

explanation.surface: It is said someone was sent out to look for a water source.
explanation.definitionFit: Dowsing is using a rod to find underground water.

clue.text: They have big clothes items old boy stuffed in drawers inappropriately

indicators.note: the old boy is pushed into the middle of the jumbled drawers letters
inappropriately says the combined letters are put in the wrong order

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: An old boy is crammed indecently into a chest of drawers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawers' is anagram fodder, not underwear: 'inappropriately' rearranges it to WARDRES, and 'stuffed in' puts OB inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Wardrobes are tall cupboards where coats and suits hang.

clue.text: Squat in small enclosed space

definitions.meaning: ..., an adjective, means short and plump
a ..., or cubbyhole, is a small snug nook

explanation.surface: Someone squatting in a tiny cramped room.
explanation.definitionFit: Cubby describes a stocky figure, and is a snug little cupboard or nook.

clue.text: Plant arrived — car turned up for collection

indicators.note: the arrived word collects the car inside it

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: in a down clue, turned up says the car word is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a limo is a limousine

explanation.surface: A plant has arrived after a car came to pick it up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turned up' reverses the car, and 'for collection' means the arrived word gathers it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Camomile is a daisy-like herb used for soothing tea.

clue.text: Walk ostentatiously to show support

explanation.surface: Parade around to demonstrate your backing.
explanation.definitionFit: Swaggering is strutting, and a structural brace is a strut.

clue.text: Student now sadly denied university time, being this?

definitions.text: Student now sadly denied university time, being this?

indicators.note: sadly says the remaining letters are mixed up
denied says the letters for university and time are withheld

explanation.surface: A student is unhappily refused more time at university, being expelled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'denied' drops U and T from STUDENT NOW; 'sadly' rearranges what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: To be sent down is to be expelled from a British university.

clue.text: Dickensian character's feeling of resentment, heading off

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter

parts.note: a grudge is lingering resentment

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure bears a grudge and goes off.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the title figure of a Dickens novel.

clue.text: In Ireland I am reminded about mythical creature

indicators.note: about tells us the concealed letters run backwards
in says the answer is concealed within the following words

explanation.surface: In Ireland, someone is put in mind of a legendary being.
explanation.definitionFit: A mermaid is a legendary sea being, half woman and half fish.

clue.text: Last messages for couple seen round India

indicators.note: the French phrase is placed around the India letter

parts.note: a deux is French for for two, a couple
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Farewell notes for a pair seen touring India.
explanation.definitionFit: Adieux are goodbyes, the final words on parting.

clue.text: Pants giving legal summaries

definitions.meaning: a brief summarises a case for a barrister

explanation.surface: Underwear issuing court documents.
explanation.definitionFit: Short underpants and a barrister's case papers are both called briefs.

clue.text: OTT party type could make Tories err

indicators.note: could make says the letters of these words may be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: An over-the-top partygoer might lead Conservatives astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests politics, given the Tories, but means a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is a noisy reveller, an over-the-top partier.

clue.text: Work out where area of fear is

parts.note: where something is, it is in somewhere

indicators.note: of is read as 'out of': the area letter is taken out of the word fear

explanation.surface: Deduce where the zone of dread lies.
explanation.walkthrough: Really a description of the answer: the area letter of the word fear sits inside the answer's last three letters. 'of' does duty as 'out of', and 'is' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: To infer is to deduce, to reason something out from evidence.

clue.text: African mothers sitting by major road

parts.note: ma is mother, so mas is mothers
the A1 is Britain's longest road, written AI

explanation.surface: African women sit at the side of a big highway.
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is the main road from London to Edinburgh; its 1 is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The Masai are a people of Kenya and Tanzania.

clue.text: Bad film of oil obliterating lake

indicators.note: obliterating says the lake letter is wiped out

parts.note: an oil slick is a film of oil on water

explanation.surface: A nasty oil spill wipes out a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sick, as in 'a sick joke', means in bad taste.

clue.text: Generation after former Labour leader shown in bit of film

indicators.note: after puts the generation behind the leader

parts.note: Michael Foot led the British Labour Party 1980-83
an age is a generation

explanation.surface: A clip shows an old political leader with a new generation.
explanation.definitionFit: Footage is recorded film material.

clue.text: Talk from the French priest about origin of temptation

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: about says the priest wraps around the next letter

parts.note: a curé is a French parish priest

indicators.note: origin of picks the first letter of temptation

explanation.surface: A French clergyman preaching on where temptation comes from.
explanation.definitionFit: A lecture is a formal talk.

clue.text: Exceptional dearness expressed primarily in these songs?

indicators.note: exceptional suggests something out of the ordinary, so the letters are rearranged
primarily picks the first letter of expressed

explanation.surface: Love songs in which unusual tenderness comes through.
explanation.definitionFit: A serenade is a love song sung under a window.
